A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAP-Net work. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A-F support comparison; the appendix pages are unchanged.

before.justification: v1 reports original RGBD-Art and OPD-real evaluations, ablations, qualitative comparisons and robotic manipulation outcomes, including Tables 2-11.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies and reports revised baseline values and different qualitative comparisons.

M1.justification: The SAM2/FeatUp feature fusion, PointNet++ backbone, three prediction heads, training losses, clustering and pose-fitting procedures remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both evaluate RGBD-Art seen/unseen objects, OPD-real and real-world robotic manipulation. The different Figure 5 examples remain within the existing RGB-D tasks and domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Table 2 retains SoftGroup, AutoGPart and GAPartNet, while the pose, OPD-real and robotic comparisons also retain their original baselines.

E3.justification: The reported training budget, image and point-cloud preprocessing, segmentation and pose metrics, symmetry treatment, and robotic success criteria are unchanged. Figure 5 introduces no different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: Figure 5 supplies different qualitative comparisons illustrating GAPartNet's 180-degree orientation errors and missed detections. The earlier examples remain in Figure 9; component ablations and appendix analyses of small parts, symmetry and inference speed are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain the same robotic trial counts and success fractions. Neither introduces additional seed information, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 2 changes SoftGroup's unseen round-fixed-handle AP50 from 5.2 to 0.05 and its average AP50 from 3.21 to 2.64. CAP-Net's numerical results remain unchanged. Figure 5 also presents different example-level qualitative results.

T1.justification: The pose/NPCS definitions and mathematical loss formulations, including Equations 1-3, are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about unified RGB-D part-pose estimation, the RGBD-Art dataset, baseline outperformance and synthetic-to-real transfer.

C2.justification: Figure 5 explicitly states that ground-truth pose annotations are unavailable for its real-world examples, clarifying the evidential limit of those comparisons. The global-context interpretation and the conclusion's missing-depth limitation remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Implementation details, loss weights, hardware, preprocessing, robotic setup and manipulation instructions are unchanged. Both retain the same dataset, code and pretrained-model access statement and project link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and 54-reference bibliography are unchanged.

P1.justification: The body prose, section order and appendix organization remain unchanged. Textual edits are limited to the arXiv version/date stamp and Figure 5 labels.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redesigned with separate synthetic and real-world blocks, different examples, reordered rows, and explicit error and ground-truth-availability labels. Its original panel remains in Figure 9; other figures and table structures are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 replaces a redundant Figure 5 panel with more informative qualitative comparisons that distinguish synthetic from real-world data, illustrate baseline failures and disclose unavailable real-world ground truth. This modestly improves evidential clarity while preserving the earlier examples in Figure 9. The method, evaluation protocols and main quantitative evidence remain essentially unchanged.
